chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother, from his father, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who does not know how many he has prayed—one, two, or three. He said: He builds upon certainty, performs the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, and recites a light tashahhud.

So it does not contradict the first two reports, because he said: he builds upon certainty, and what certainty requires is recommencing the salat (prayer), as we have explained. The command to perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness is therefore understood as recommendation, not as compensation for the salat (prayer).

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Abā al-Ḥasan, peace be upon him
key_terms.لِجُبْرَانِ الصَّلَاةِ: to compensate for a deficiency in the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if he does not know whether he has prayed one, two, or three rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for one who is uncertain whether he has prayed one, two, or three rak'ahs. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to act on certainty, while the compiler explains that this means restarting the salat (prayer), and that sajdatay al-sahw here are understood as recommended rather than compensatory.
